title: Bootstrap plan is deny-by-default and preserves provenance
statement: Each devai init apply-* mutation MUST NOT overwrite existing files unless --force is set, and even with --force the provenance-critical files (.devai/state/evidence-chain.json and .devai/state/counters.json) MUST be preserved when they contain real data (chain.records non-empty or any counter > 0). Each ExecuteResult MUST surface preserved paths separately from overwritten ones.
rationale: Article 36 makes the framework's ability to apply to itself a binding constraint; the evidence chain is the framework's auditable substrate. A `--force` flag that silently clobbers the chain or counters destroys the very provenance that proves self-application. Every role-separated bootstrap apply path must be deny-by-default for existing files and explicitly preserve the provenance-critical subset even under --force.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
